title: Cannonball Adderley's joke and Procope's refusal to recreate Kirby
summary: Cannonball Adderley teased him about Benny Carter on the Kirby tribute; Procope says he turned down a request to recreate the band, since it cannot be redone.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Cannonball Adderley: the sound, the man, the band

blocks.x: So they took the solos too, as I recall.
I think Benny Carter played the --
Yeah. And this fellow -- what's the alto player's name? The two brothers, the trumpet player and the --

Cannonball. Cannonball Adderly. So he came over to me, and we were sitting and talking one day, so he was kidding me, he said, 'Who came first, Russell Procope or Benny Carter?' You know. That sort of thing is -- it's all right, I guess, you know.
It's strange, you know, that you being around, that they didn't get you.
I guess they knew better. They knew better. Just like here recently, George Wein and the fellow over at the -- I can't ever remember the name of that place.
What's the jazz place on the east side?
No. The -- the place Clark Terry's playing in now. Well, anyway, they wanted me to recreate the --
Yes, that's right, he opened there. I don't mean that. I don't mean Storytown. It's a place where Benny Carter plays when he comes to town.

Well, anyway, they wanted me to recreate it, so I told them no. I said it would be impossible. Now, I mean you could get people if you could get the arrangements from somewhere, I don't know where. You could play the music. But to my mind, you know, when you're listening to it and you know what -- like you know, you know how it was at one time, I wouldn't be at all satisfied to try to do that. No, impossible.
It doesn't make any sense either.
